title: The unipotent Frobenius-kernel distribution socle
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel to $S$ is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B$. A split torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$, with $\mathbf G_m(D)=D^\times$; maximal means maximal under inclusion; Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Its unipotent radical is its largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, with unipotent meaning unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Use the character lattice $X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and the positive roots $\Phi^+$ in the tangent space $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, with roots interpreted as torus characters, as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $N=|\Phi^+|$. Fix $r\ge1$ and $q=p^r$. For each affine $F$-group $K$, put $K^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(F[K]\otimes_{F,a\mapsto a^q}F)$ and $K_r=\ker(F^r_{K/F}:K\to K^{(q)})$, where the relative Frobenius has coordinate map $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a finite such kernel put $\operatorname{Dist}(K_r)=\operatorname{Hom}_F(F[K_r],F)$, with convolution product $(ab)(f)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta f)$, unit evaluation at the identity, augmentation $a\mapsto a(1)$ and antipode $\sigma$ dual to inversion; these agree with the finite-order distributions of [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus]. Put $U=R_u(B)$ and $H=\operatorname{Dist}(U_r)$. Choose any enumeration $\Phi^+=\{\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N\}$ without repetitions and root parametrizations $x_{\beta_i}:\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{\beta_i}$ [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Their restrictions to the $r$th kernels define distributions
$$d_{\beta_i}^{(n)}(f)=[t^n]x_{\beta_i}^*f\qquad(0\le n<q),$$
where the pullback is in $F[t]/(t^q)$. The ordered monomials $\prod_{i=1}^N d_{\beta_i}^{(a_i)}$ with $0\le a_i<q$ are an $F$-basis of $H$. Let $J=\{h\in H:h(1)=0\}$ and $z=\prod_{i=1}^N d_{\beta_i}^{(q-1)}$. There is an integer $m\ge1$ with $J^m=0$, and
$$\{h\in H:jh=0\text{ for every }j\in J\}=Fz,\qquad z\ne0.$$
The assertion applies also to the unipotent radical of any opposite Borel subgroup, meaning a Borel subgroup $B^-\supseteq T$ with $B\cap B^-=T$, with its negative roots $-\Phi^+$, root subgroups $U_{-\beta_i}$ and parametrizations $x_{-\beta_i}:\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{-\beta_i}$ [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] in place of $\Phi^+$, $U_{\beta_i}$ and $x_{\beta_i}$. For $N=0$ it says $H=F$, $J=0$ and $z=1$.

source.place: Agent formulation of the higher-kernel version of the unipotent PBW/local-socle input to Jantzen II.3.18, with general distribution background I.8-I.9. Local book WANTED; no exact book lemma claimed read.

proof.text: The last sentence of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] makes $S$ reductive. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and the chosen parametrizations, $\mu:\mathbf A_F^N\to U$, $(t_i)\mapsto\prod_i x_{\beta_i}(t_i)$, is a pointed scheme isomorphism. Thus $F[U]=F[t_1,\ldots,t_N]$, with identity $t_i=0$. In these coordinates the displayed relative Frobenius pulls each twisted coordinate back to $t_i^q$. Its fibre over the identity therefore has coordinate algebra $C=F[U_r]=F[t_1,\ldots,t_N]/(t_1^q,\ldots,t_N^q)$. The monomials $t^a$, $0\leq a_i<q$, are a basis: reducing exponents gives spanning, and the ideal generated by the $t_i^q$ is spanned by precisely the excluded monomials, giving independence. This proves in particular that $U_r$ is finite.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a), p.445 and Remark 21.69, p.446; the relative-Frobenius fibre calculation is agent-written from the coordinate formula in the item.

proof.text: Let $e_a=\prod_i d_{\beta_i}^{(a_i)}$. By the convolution definition [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus], evaluation of $e_a$ on $f\in C$ is the coefficient $[t_1^{a_1}\cdots t_N^{a_N}]\mu^*f$: the iterated coproduct is pullback along iterated multiplication, and applying the root coefficient functionals extracts that coefficient. This identity also follows inductively from $(ab)(f)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta f)$, adding one factor at a time. Hence $e_a(t^b)=\delta_{a,b}$. The $e_a$ are the dual basis, $z=e_{(q-1,\ldots,q-1)}\ne0$, and $e_0$ is the unit. Since $\epsilon(t_i)=0$, $\ker\epsilon=(t_1,\ldots,t_N)$ and $(\ker\epsilon)^{N(q-1)+1}=0$ in $C$, so every functional is a finite-order distribution and $H$ is the algebra of [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus] for $U_r$. Evaluating on $1=t^0$ shows that $J$ is the span of the $e_a$ with $a\ne0$.

source.place: Chapter 10 distribution convolution construction; coefficient extraction along the root product is written out, using step 1.

proof.text: Choose a regular cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ with $B=P(\lambda)$ by [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description]. Its displayed tangent-space formula and the definition of $\Phi^+$ give $d_i=\langle\beta_i,\lambda\rangle>0$. The conjugation formula of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], together with the $T$-equivariance in [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], scales the $i$th chart coordinate by $s^{d_i}$. It preserves $(t_i^q)$, so defines conjugation on $U_r$. Pushing a distribution forward under conjugation gives $\lambda(s)e_a=s^{\sum_i a_i d_i}e_a$. Since conjugation respects multiplication in $U_r$, convolution of vectors of degrees $u,v$ has degree $u+v$. Explicitly, expanding the product in the basis and comparing Laurent coefficients of $s$ forces its coefficient at $e_c$ to vanish unless $\sum_i c_i d_i=u+v$. This works as a character identity over $F[s,s^{-1}]$, including when two character differentials coincide in characteristic $p$.

source.place: Theorem 21.32 and Definition 21.35, pp.434--435; root conjugation 21.19, p.431; Theorem 21.68(a), p.445. Degree bookkeeping is agent-written.

proof.text: Put $M=(q-1)\sum_i d_i$. Every basis vector in $J$ has degree at least $1$, while no basis vector has degree greater than $M$. Expanding a product of $M+1$ elements of $J$ into homogeneous basis products therefore gives zero. Thus $J^{M+1}=0$; the augmentation is multiplicative since $\Delta(1)=1\otimes1$, so $J$ is a two-sided ideal. The vector $z$ has degree $M$, so the same degree calculation gives $Jz=0$. If $N=0$, $M=0$ and the coordinate basis already gives $H=F$, $J=0$ and $z=1$, with nilpotence exponent $1$.

source.place: Agent degree argument from steps 2--3; no structure theorem about local or Hopf algebras is used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] to the affine group $U_r$. Its coordinate maps give exactly the unital algebra coproduct and counit identities required by [lem-sfb-truncated-coordinate-convolution-pairing]; in the chart the counit sends each $t_i$ to $0$. The pairing lemma therefore says that, for $\omega=\prod_i t_i^{q-1}$ and $L(h)=h(\omega)$, $L(ah)=0$ for every $a\in H$ implies $h=0$. Step 2 gives $L(z)=1$. If $Jh=0$, then $a-a(1)1_H\in J$ for every $a\in H$, hence $ah=a(1)h$. Since $Jz=0$, the element $k=h-L(h)z$ also satisfies $Jk=0$ and $L(k)=0$. Consequently $L(ak)=a(1)L(k)=0$ for every $a$, and nondegeneracy forces $k=0$. This proves $\{h:Jh=0\}=Fz$.

source.place: Affine group coordinate Hopf axioms and agent top-coordinate pairing; the annihilator calculation is explicit. Jantzen I.8-I.9 and II.3.18 remain WANTED, not claimed read.

proof.text: Let $B^-\supseteq T$ be a Borel subgroup with $B\cap B^-=T$ and $\Psi$ the roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B^-)$. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] take regular $\lambda,\mu$ with $B=P(\lambda)$, $B^-=P(\mu)$, so $\Phi^+=\{\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0\}$ and $\Psi=\{\langle\alpha,\mu\rangle>0\}$. As $s_\alpha(\alpha)=-\alpha$ [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $\Phi=-\Phi$, hence $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup-\Phi^+=\Psi\sqcup-\Psi$. Tangent spaces of a scheme-theoretic intersection intersect (dual-number points), so $\operatorname{Lie}(B)\cap\operatorname{Lie}(B^-)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)$ and $\Phi^+\cap\Psi=\varnothing$. Thus $\Psi\subseteq-\Phi^+$ and $-\Psi\subseteq\Phi^+$, so $\Psi=-\Phi^+$. Apply steps 1--5 to $(T,B^-)$ with $-\beta_1,\ldots,-\beta_N$, the parametrizations $x_{-\beta_i}$ and $\mu$: [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] holds for every Borel pair, and $\langle-\beta_i,\mu\rangle>0$. This proves every clause for $R_u(B^-)$, including $N=0$.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a) and Remark 21.69 applied to the opposite Borel pair; no identification of positive and negative distribution algebras is assumed.
